analysis.estimand: Whether the parent ablation's toggle-induced ranking-shift for a fixed solver pair exceeds the 95th percentile of the same ranking-shift statistic's empirical distribution under seed-only resampling of the identical control plan.
analysis.population: The one solver pair, instance family/size/parameters, lambda grid and tolerance set used in the parent ablation's untoggled control cell.
analysis.target_claim: The parent ablation's reported ranking shift for this solver pair is no larger than ordinary seed-resampling noise, so the toggle is not shown to cause it.
analysis.unanalysable_reason: The idea's central quantity is a comparison between (a) a noise-floor statistic computed here and (b) the parent ablation's already-computed toggle-induced ranking-shift for the same pair. (b) is not a declared observable: cg.cells@1's solves records carry no field recording a toggle condition, a protocol variant, or any already-computed shift magnitude, and no capability in the catalogue exposes the parent ablation's result as a readable scalar or record set. There is therefore no observable from which the comparison the idea's falsifier depends on -- "does the toggle-induced shift exceed this threshold" -- could ever be evaluated; freezing a guessed numeric threshold in its place would not be measuring the parent ablation's result, it would be inventing one. Separately, even the noise-floor half is not expressible: the idea defines its statistic per execution (aggregated over one execution's instance x lambda_ratio x tolerance grid) and wants the distribution of that per-execution scalar across ~30 independently seeded executions. The declared reduction operations (count, fraction, mean, median, std, min, max, sum, quantile, difference, ratio, correlation, ols_coefficient) act once over a single flat set of records -- the campaign's solves concatenated across units -- with no grouping construct and no field identifying which unit/execution a record came from (seed and instance_label vary per instance, not per unit, and campaign unit boundaries are not themselves a readable field). So a distribution of per-execution statistic values, as opposed to one statistic computed over all pooled records, cannot be formed from what cg.cells@1 declares. Both gaps would need to close -- a readable parent-ablation shift value, and a per-execution grouping field -- before this idea's prediction could be measured; neither is present in the observable catalogue.

hypothesis.core_idea: Before attributing a ranking shift between two solvers to a protocol toggle, measure how much the same ranking-shift statistic moves under zero toggle, using repeated fresh instance draws (new RESEARCH_OS_SEED_0 per execution, not bootstrap-reweighting of one fixed small instance set) as the sole noise source, since the capability declares solver execution paths deterministic given plan and seed -- the only seed-driven randomness is in instance generation, not in solver algorithms.
hypothesis.falsifier: Run ~30 executions of the identical control plan (same solver pair, family, size, lambda grid, tolerances) differing only in RESEARCH_OS_SEED_0, compute the solver-pair ranking-shift statistic per execution, and derive its empirical 95th-percentile magnitude. If the parent ablation's toggle-induced shift for that same pair exceeds this threshold, sampling noise is rejected as the explanation; if the toggle-induced shift falls at or below this threshold, noise is confirmed as a sufficient alternative explanation for that ablation result.
hypothesis.mechanism: cg.cells@1 caps each execution at 2 distinct solvers ('arms'), so the statistic is scoped to one solver pair at a time (the pair from the parent ablation), computed from each execution's 'solves' records (objective, ok, wall_seconds) aggregated across that execution's instance x lambda_ratio x tolerance grid. A campaign (or several, since a single campaign caps at 6 execution-units) supplies ~30 such executions, each an independent fresh instance draw under an unchanged plan; the resulting ~30 statistic values form the empirical null. This replaces the original bootstrap-of-a-fixed-4-instance-set with genuine resampling of the instance population via the seed offset, and replaces the 'solver seed' assumption (unsupported by the declared determinism) with instance-generation seed as the only verified noise source.
hypothesis.research_question: Holding the plan fixed at exactly the parent ablation's untoggled control cell (same two solvers, same instance family/size/parameters, same lambda grid and tolerances) and varying only RESEARCH_OS_SEED_0 across repeated executions, what is the empirical distribution of the solver-pair ranking-shift statistic, and does the toggle-induced shift reported in the parent ablation for that same pair exceed its 95th percentile?
hypothesis.title: Seed-resampling noise floor for a single solver-pair ranking-shift statistic
